note: Accounting for every assertion identifier published in the W3C SOAP 1.2 test collection, revalidated against the pinned Second Edition text. See verify_ledger.py for the rules this file must satisfy.

normative_quotes: For an implementation to claim conformance with the SOAP Version 1.2 specification, it MUST correctly implement all mandatory ("MUST") requirements expressed in Part 1 of the SOAP Version 1.2 specification (this document) that pertain to the activity being performed. Note that an implementation is not mandated to implement all the mandatory requirements.
assertions.rationale: Section 1.2 states the conformance obligation that ranges over the other mandatory requirements of Part 1; it describes no distinct observable behavior of its own. Every mandatory Part 1 requirement it ranges over is itself a row in this ledger, so testing this row separately would only re-assert those rows.

normative_quotes: The implementation of an Adjunct MUST implement all the pertinent mandatory requirements expressed in the specification of the Adjunct to claim conformance with the Adjunct.
assertions.rationale: As with the Part 1 conformance statement, this ranges over the mandatory requirements of Part 2 rather than describing its own behavior. The Part 2 requirements are separately rowed here, including the encoding and RPC requirements routed to P8.

normative_quotes: SOAP does not require that XML Schema processing (assessment or validation) be performed to establish the correctness or 'schema implied' values of element and attribute information items defined by Parts 1 and 2 of this specification. The values associated with element and attribute information items defined in this specification MUST be carried explicitly in the transmitted SOAP message except where stated otherwise (see 5. SOAP Message Construct).
assertions.rationale: A receiver must accept a conforming envelope without schema validation being required. The known-good corpus decodes third-party envelopes and the envelope suite accepts valid namespace scopes, neither of which imposes schema validation on the envelope.

tests.case: Round-trip validation
Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content

normative_quotes: Unless otherwise stated, all lexical forms are supported for each such attribute, and lexical forms representing the same value in the XML Schema value space are considered equivalent for purposes of SOAP processing, e.g.
the boolean lexical forms "1" and "true" are interchangeable.
assertions.rationale: Lexical forms carried in a SOAP message must be preserved as XML lexical values. Special-character and round-trip coverage exercises the lexical forms directly.

tests.case: Corner cases: special characters
Round-trip validation

normative_quotes: A SOAP node receiving a SOAP message MUST perform processing according to the SOAP processing model as described in this section and in the remainder of this specification.
assertions.rationale: A node must implement the processing model for the roles it acts in. The node truth table drives every role/capability/mandatory/relay combination, and the HTTP case drives the same node through real client and handler transports.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Clients and handlers process targeted headers before application data

normative_quotes: The roles assumed by a node MUST be invariant during the processing of an individual SOAP message.
assertions.rationale: Roles must be invariant while a message is processed. Node capabilities are immutable after construction and the concurrency case asserts that concurrent calls share them without observing a change mid-message.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Concurrent calls share immutable capabilities and isolate results

normative_quotes: Table 2: SOAP Roles defined by this specification Short-name Name Description next "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/role/next" Each SOAP intermediary and the ultimate SOAP receiver MUST act in this role.
assertions.rationale: The next role must be assumed by every intermediary and ultimate receiver. The truth table includes headers targeted at next for both node kinds.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table

normative_quotes: none "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/role/none" SOAP nodes MUST NOT act in this role.
assertions.rationale: No node may act in the none role, so a header targeted at it is never understood or processed by this node; the truth table covers that targeting.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table

normative_quotes: ultimateReceiver "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/role/ultimateReceiver" The ultimate receiver MUST act in this role.
assertions.rationale: The ultimate receiver must assume the ultimateReceiver role; the truth table drives headers targeted at it against both ultimate-receiver and intermediary configurations.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table

normative_quotes: Mandatory SOAP header blocks are presumed to somehow modify the semantics of other SOAP header blocks or SOAP body elements. Therefore, for every mandatory SOAP header block targeted to a node, that node MUST either process the header block or not process the SOAP message at all, and instead generate a fault (see 2.6 Processing SOAP Messages and 5.4 SOAP Fault).
assertions.rationale: A header block with mustUnderstand true targeted at the node must be understood or else generate a fault. Both the truth table and the processing-priority suite assert the MustUnderstand fault for an unknown targeted mandatory header.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Mandatory headers precede body faults for each version and node role

normative_quotes: In particular, it is not an error for an ultimate SOAP receiver to receive a message containing a mandatory SOAP header block that is targeted at a role other than the ones assumed by the ultimate SOAP receiver.
assertions.rationale: The obligation falls on the node acting as ultimate receiver; the preflight case shows the mandatory check running before application callbacks and recovering afterwards.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Mandatory preflight precedes callbacks; failures are recoverable

assertions.section_title: Structure and Interpretation of SOAP Bodies
normative_quotes: An ultimate SOAP receiver MUST correctly process the immediate children of the SOAP body (see 5.3 SOAP Body).
assertions.rationale: An ultimate receiver must correctly process the immediate children of the Body. Body part selection drives single, multiple and explicitly empty body children.

tests.case: One and multiple selected parts determine wire values
Explicit empty bodies preserve native and retained values

normative_quotes: Unless otherwise stated, processing of all generated SOAP messages, SOAP faults and application-level side effects MUST be semantically equivalent to performing the following steps separately, and in the order given.
Determine the set of roles in which the node is to act.
The contents of the SOAP envelope, including any SOAP header blocks and the SOAP body, MAY be inspected in making such determination.
assertions.rationale: Generated messages must be semantically equivalent to performing the listed steps in order. The ordering that is observable to a peer - role determination, mandatory-header checking, then Body processing - is asserted by the truth table and the priority suite.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Mandatory headers precede body faults for each version and node role

normative_quotes: In all cases where a SOAP header block is processed, the SOAP node MUST understand the SOAP header block and MUST do such processing in a manner fully conformant with the specification for that header block.
assertions.rationale: Header blocks must be processed according to their own specifications; header processors registered with the node receive exactly their targeted blocks.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Clients and handlers process targeted headers before application data

normative_quotes: An ultimate SOAP receiver MUST process the SOAP body, in a manner consistent with 2.5 Structure and Interpretation of SOAP Bodies.
assertions.rationale: Body processing belongs to the ultimate receiver and follows header processing; the priority case asserts an invalid Body still rejects only after header handling.

tests.case: One and multiple selected parts determine wire values
Invalid bodies still reject before known header callbacks

normative_quotes: Failure is indicated by the generation of a fault (see 5.4 SOAP Fault).
assertions.rationale: A node that generates a fault must stop ordinary processing of the message. The handler-fault case asserts that a fault terminates processing and returns the correct code rather than continuing to application output.

tests.case: Mandatory headers precede body faults for each version and node role
Application, output and declared fault failures retain correct codes and recovery

normative_quotes: The selection of a fault need not be predicated on the application of the "MUST", "SHOULD" or "MAY" keywords to the generation of the fault, with the exception that if one or more of the prescribed faults is qualified with the "MUST" keyword, then any one fault from the set of possible faults MUST be generated.
assertions.rationale: Where more than one fault is possible the node may choose; the priority suite fixes the documented choice - mandatory-header faults precede Body faults - for each version and role, so the choice is deterministic rather than arbitrary.

tests.case: Mandatory headers precede body faults for each version and node role
Generic, declared and header faults support explicit protocol fields

normative_quotes: A SOAP header block MAY carry a relay attribute information item (see 5.2.4 SOAP relay Attribute).
assertions.rationale: Relayable header blocks must survive forwarding when not processed. The truth table covers the relay attribute and the forwarding case asserts retention and order.

tests.case: Role, capability, mandatory and relay truth table
Forwarding preserves order, XML context and body values

normative_quotes: Forwarding SOAP intermediaries MUST process the message according to the SOAP processing model defined in 2.6 Processing SOAP Messages. In addition, when generating a SOAP message for the purpose of forwarding, they MUST: Remove all processed SOAP header blocks. Remove all non-relayable SOAP header blocks that were targeted at the forwarding node but ignored during processing. Retain all relayable SOAP header blocks that were targeted at the forwarding node but ignored during processing.
assertions.rationale: A forwarding intermediary must process the message under the ordinary processing model and then forward it; the forwarding case drives exactly that sequence.

tests.case: Forwarding preserves order, XML context and body values

normative_quotes: Forwarding SOAP intermediaries MUST process the message according to the SOAP processing model defined in 2.6 Processing SOAP Messages.
assertions.rationale: The Second Edition states the forwarding obligation as conformance to the processing model of section 2.6 rather than to a separately specified forwarding feature, so the testable requirement is the processing-model behavior the forwarding case asserts.

tests.case: Forwarding preserves order, XML context and body values

assertions.superseded: The 2003 collection quotes a First Edition sentence requiring conformance to "the specification for the SOAP forwarding feature being used"; the Second Edition instead requires conformance to the section 2.6 processing model.

normative_quotes: The element information item for a header block targeted at an intermediary MAY be removed, by that intermediary, from the [children] property of the SOAP Header element information item as detailed in 2.7.2 SOAP Forwarding Intermediaries.
Element information items for additional header blocks MAY be added to the [children] property of the SOAP Header element information item as detailed in 2.7.2 SOAP Forwarding Intermediaries.
Comment information items MAY be added to the [children] property of the SOAP Envelope element information item.
assertions.rationale: All infoset properties must be preserved across relaying apart from the listed header exceptions; the forwarding case asserts order, XML context and body values survive.

tests.case: Forwarding preserves order, XML context and body values

assertions.superseded: The collection cites section 2.7.4, which does not exist in the Second Edition; the relayed-infoset requirement is section 2.7.2.1.

normative_quotes: A SOAP node determines whether it supports the version of a SOAP message on a per message basis.
assertions.rationale: Version is determined per message by the envelope namespace; the mismatch case asserts a selected version rejects the other namespace without affecting the next decode.

tests.case: Selected versions reject mismatches without changing the next decode
Version negotiation faults preserve SOAP 1.1 transition semantics

normative_quotes: A SOAP node MAY support multiple envelope versions. However, when processing a message, a SOAP node MUST use the semantics defined by the version of that message.
assertions.rationale: The envelope namespace names the version; valid scopes are accepted and an envelope in an unrecognized namespace is rejected.

tests.case: Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content
Invalid envelope namespace rejected

normative_quotes: If a SOAP node receives a message whose version is not supported it MUST generate a fault (see 5.4 SOAP Fault) with a Value of Code set to "env:VersionMismatch". Any other malformation of the message construct MUST result in the generation of a fault with a Value of Code set to "env:Sender".
assertions.rationale: A node receiving an unsupported envelope version must generate a VersionMismatch fault; the version-negotiation case asserts the fault and its SOAP 1.1 transition behavior.

tests.case: Version negotiation faults preserve SOAP 1.1 transition semantics
Empty values, long subcode chains and version negotiation keep their identities

normative_quotes: The processing of SOAP envelopes in accordance with the SOAP Processing Model (see 2. SOAP Processing Model) MUST NOT be overridden by binding specifications.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. This implementation defines no feature, module or binding of its own and uses the SOAP HTTP binding specified in Part 2 section 7, so there is no artifact of ours for the requirement to constrain.

normative_quotes: The specification of a feature MUST include the following: A URI used to name the feature. This enables the feature to be unambiguously referenced in description languages or during negotiation. The information (state) required at each node to implement the feature. The processing required at each node in order to fulfill the obligations of the feature including any handling of communication failures that might occur in the underlying protocol (see also 4.2 Binding Framework). The information to be transmitted from node to node.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. This implementation defines no feature, module or binding of its own and uses the SOAP HTTP binding specified in Part 2 section 7, so there is no artifact of ours for the requirement to constrain.

normative_quotes: An MEP specification MUST also include: Any requirements to generate additional messages (such as responses to requests in a request/response MEP). Rules for the delivery or other disposition of SOAP faults generated during the operation of the MEP.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. MUST identify itself with a URI.
This enables the module to be unambiguously referenced in description languages or during negotiation.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. This implementation defines no feature, module or binding of its own and uses the SOAP HTTP binding specified in Part 2 section 7, so there is no artifact of ours for the requirement to constrain.

normative_quotes: A binding specification MUST enable one or more MEPs.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. This implementation defines no feature, module or binding of its own and uses the SOAP HTTP binding specified in Part 2 section 7, so there is no artifact of ours for the requirement to constrain.

normative_quotes: In cases where multiple features are supported by a binding specification, the specifications for those features MUST provide any information necessary for their successful use in combination.
assertions.rationale: This requirement is addressed to the specification that defines a SOAP feature, module or protocol binding, not to a node implementing one. normative_quotes: However, the binding framework does not require that every binding use an XML serialization for transmission; compressed, encrypted, fragmented representations and so on can be used if appropriate.
assertions.rationale: This is a permission granted to binding specifications, not an obligation on a node: it states that a binding need not use an XML serialization. This implementation uses the HTTP binding, which does use an XML serialization, so the permission imposes nothing testable here.
assertions.superseded: The First Edition wording quoted by the collection says "the XML 1.0 [8] serialization"; the Second Edition generalizes it to "an XML serialization for transmission".

normative_quotes: Although streaming SOAP receivers will acquire such XML infosets incrementally, SOAP processing MUST yield results identical to those that would have been achieved if the entire SOAP envelope were available prior to the start of processing.
assertions.rationale: A receiver that acquires the infoset incrementally must still produce results identical to processing a complete envelope. The duplex suite streams a request whose response is delivered while the request is still being sent, and asserts the decoded value matches.

tests.case: Buffered requests complete against early responses in every graph and value mode
Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content

assertions.superseded: The Second Edition rewords the surrounding streaming discussion; the identical-results obligation is unchanged and is what is quoted here.

normative_quotes: This element information item is also the value of the [document element] property.
assertions.rationale: The envelope document information item must have exactly the SOAP Envelope element as its child; malformed containers are rejected before any payload decoding.

tests.case: Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content
Malformed containers reject before native or retained payload decoding

normative_quotes: The [notations] and [unparsed entities] properties are both empty.
assertions.rationale: The SOAP infoset must correspond to an XML 1.0 serialization. Round-trip and known-good coverage asserts the envelopes this implementation emits and accepts are XML 1.0 serializable rather than merely reporting an XML version.

tests.case: Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content
Round-trip validation

assertions.superseded: The collection adds a First Edition sentence about standalone="yes" or absent, which the Second Edition section 5 does not carry; a standalone="no" declaration is therefore not rejected on that basis.

normative_quotes: The XML infoset of a SOAP message MUST NOT contain a document type declaration information item.
assertions.rationale: A SOAP message must not carry a DTD; the wire-document case asserts DTDs reject in SOAP mode while remaining permissible for ordinary XML handling.

tests.case: Wire documents reject DTDs and processing instructions only in SOAP mode

normative_quotes: SOAP messages sent by initial SOAP senders MUST NOT contain processing instruction information items. SOAP intermediaries MUST NOT insert processing instruction information items in SOAP messages they relay. SOAP receivers receiving a SOAP message containing a processing instruction information item SHOULD generate a SOAP fault with the Value of Code set to "env:Sender".
assertions.rationale: A SOAP message must not carry processing instructions; asserted by the same wire-document case, which distinguishes SOAP mode from ordinary XML parsing.

tests.case: Wire documents reject DTDs and processing instructions only in SOAP mode

normative_quotes: The SOAP Envelope element information item has:
A [local name] of Envelope.
A [namespace name] of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope".
assertions.rationale: The Envelope element information item properties - local name, namespace, children - are asserted on both decoding and serialization.

tests.case: Both versions preserve valid envelope namespace scopes and content
Serialization rejects unqualified compatibility headers and containers

normative_quotes: The encodingStyle attribute information item has: A [local name] of encodingStyle. A [namespace name] of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope". The encodingStyle attribute information item is of type xs:anyURI.
assertions.rationale: The encodingStyle attribute properties are asserted where encoding styles are carried on headers and on the fault application/protocol boundary.

tests.case: Fault encodingStyle placement matches the SOAP application/protocol boundary
Encoded headers retain independent accessor namespaces and encoding styles

normative_quotes: The encodingStyle attribute information item MAY appear on the following:
A child element information item of the SOAP Body element information item (see 5.3.1 SOAP Body child Element) if that child is not a SOAP Fault element information item (see 5.4 SOAP Fault).
A child element information item of the SOAP Detail element information item (see 5.4.5.1 SOAP detail entry).
assertions.rationale: encodingStyle is restricted in scope within a fault; the fault case asserts placement matches the application/protocol boundary.

tests.case: Fault encodingStyle placement matches the SOAP application/protocol boundary

normative_quotes: The encodingStyle attribute information item MUST NOT appear on any element other than above in a SOAP message infoset.
assertions.rationale: The attribute may appear only on the listed elements. The fault encodingStyle case asserts the permitted placements and rejects the others.

tests.case: Fault encodingStyle placement matches the SOAP application/protocol boundary

normative_quotes: If no encodingStyle attribute information item is in scope for a particular element information item or the value of such an attribute information item is "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/encoding/none" then no claims are made regarding the encoding style of that element information item and its descendants.
assertions.rationale: Absence of encodingStyle means no claim is made about encoding; asserted by the fault case, which distinguishes an absent style from an explicit one.

tests.case: Fault encodingStyle placement matches the SOAP application/protocol boundary

normative_quotes: The Header element information item has:
A [namespace name] of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope".
assertions.rationale: The Header element information item properties are asserted on decode, and only header blocks in the active SOAP namespace are treated as protocol headers.

normative_quotes: Each SOAP header block element information item:
MAY have any number of character information item children.
MAY have any number of element information item children.

normative_quotes: The role attribute information item has the following XML infoset properties: A [local name] of role. A [namespace name] of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope". A [specified] property with a value of "true". The type of the role attribute information item is xs:anyURI. The value of the role attribute information item is a URI that names a role that a SOAP node can assume.
assertions.rationale: The role attribute properties, including its anyURI type, are asserted by the truth table and by the URI-syntax case that rejects invalid references.

SOAP role and actor attributes reject invalid RFC 3986 references

normative_quotes: Omitting the SOAP role attribute information item is equivalent to supplying that attribute with a value of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/role/ultimateReceiver".
assertions.rationale: An omitted role attribute targets the ultimate receiver; the truth table includes the omitted-attribute row for both node kinds.

normative_quotes: SOAP senders SHOULD NOT generate, but SOAP receivers MUST accept, the SOAP role attribute information item with a value of "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope/role/ultimateReceiver".

normative_quotes: The Code element information item has: A [local name] of Code. A [namespace name] of http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope.
